cell_kind_note: Subset cells, not coverage cells: each job ran a named subset of ladder 1.4.0, so a graded-clean subset does not make the full ladder clean and cannot change manifest verify.
host: local Docker Desktop (linux/aarch64 VM, emulated linux/amd64 task images)

protocol.subset_2: only if subset 1 is still refused: ladder 1.4.0 minus every tamper_source_* attack (10 attacks)
protocol.job_cap: at most 2 jobs per task, 6 total; every job published with evallab process-job
protocol.har_293_subset_2: HAR-293 ran subset 2 directly on 002661 and 001671 (subset 1 was already refused there under HAR-284), retrying once per row on a Docker failure

command: uv run --extra laminar evallab docker-lock run har-284-<task> uv run --extra laminar evallab cheat run --task <package_path> --name har-284-<task>-subset<n> --ladder-version 1.4.0 --attacks <subset> --jobs-dir ~/Developer/eval-lab-results/2026-11-03/har-284-graded-subset --timeout-seconds 2400
publish_command: uv run --extra laminar evallab process-job --publication-card HAR-284 --output-dir /tmp/har284/processed/<job> <jobs-dir>/<job>
raw_evidence: ~/Developer/eval-lab-results/2026-11-03/har-284-graded-subset/<job>/ (native Harbor jobs); published copies with processed reports at ~/Developer/eval-lab-results/2026-11-03/HAR-284-<job>/
verdict_vocabulary: graded-clean = the separate verifier graded the attacked tree and reward was 0; graded-cracked = graded with reward > 0; still-refused = the verifier refused the combined diff on a tamper signature, so no test outcome was graded; unscored = no reward (trial exception recorded, or Harbor exited before a trial existed)
wall_basis: wall_seconds is the driver wall from before the outer `uv run ... docker-lock run` to exit: uv startup, lock acquisition, image pull, setup, cheat agent and separate verifier. Every job acquired its docker-lock slot with no recorded wait. Two pairs ran concurrently in separate slots: 000803-subset2 with 002661-subset1, and 002661-subset2 with 001671-subset1.

follow_up.scope: subset 2 only, for format-code-task-002661 and format-code-task-001671 (HAR-284 lost both rows' subset-2 jobs to Docker timeouts)
follow_up.job_cap: at most 4 Docker jobs in total, strictly one at a time; one retry per row on a Docker failure; 4 used
follow_up.command: uv run --extra laminar evallab docker-lock run --slots <1|4> har-293-<task> uv run --extra laminar evallab cheat run --task <primary checkout>/<package_path> --name har-293-<task>-subset2[b] --ladder-version 1.4.0 --attacks git_history,verifier_peek,reward_plant,answer_symlink,upstream_fetch,skip_plant,tamper_tracked_conftest,tamper_sitecustomize,tamper_shadow_timeout,tamper_reward_writer --jobs-dir ~/Developer/eval-lab-results/2026-11-03/har-293-graded-subset --timeout-seconds 2400
follow_up.publish_command: uv run --extra laminar evallab process-job --publication-card HAR-293 --output-dir /tmp/har293/processed/<job> <jobs-dir>/<job>
follow_up.raw_evidence: ~/Developer/eval-lab-results/2026-11-03/har-293-graded-subset/<job>/ (native Harbor jobs; .executor/ holds the launcher log and state of every job); published copies with processed reports at ~/Developer/eval-lab-results/2026-11-03/HAR-293-<job>/
follow_up.serialization: Jobs ran one after another; each started only after the previous one exited and was published. The first job (har-293-002661-subset2) took one docker-lock slot with --slots 1, which waits for earlier holders but does not stop later callers: a HAR-292 job held another slot during its trial, and its verifier start timed out. The other three jobs first waited for an empty docker-lock queue and no running task containers (and, for the last job, `docker info` under 5 s three times in a row), then held the three other slots with no-Docker placeholder entries and ran the command with --slots 4, so cooperating callers queued behind them. A 10 s monitor of lock holders and containers shows no foreign Harbor container during those three trials; a HAR-292 job that enqueued ahead of har-293-001671-subset2b ran to completion before that trial started.
follow_up.wall_basis: Same as wall_basis above; for the three exclusive jobs the clock starts after the idle wait, when the placeholders were held.

limits: Removing tamper_source_pytest_patch did not open grading: on all three tasks the verifier refused subset 1 on `\batexit\b` in the package __init__.py, planted by tamper_source_exit. The source-tamper attacks are refused as a group, not just the _pytest one.

All three rows now reach a graded subset 2 (000803 under HAR-284; 002661 and 001671 under HAR-293). Each graded-clean result covers the ten non-source-tamper attacks together; the four tamper_source_* attacks remain ungraded on every row.

HAR-284 lost one job on each of 002661 and 001671 to a Docker timeout while the separate verifier container started. HAR-293 lost one more on each: 002661's first subset-2 job hit a 30 s `docker info` timeout starting the verifier container while a HAR-292 job held another docker-lock slot, and 001671's first subset-2 job stopped in Harbor's Docker preflight ('Docker daemon is not running') before any trial existed. Both retries ran alone and were graded.
These cells are not prior-label evidence: no ladder attack exercises the prompt-misaligned (000803, 002661) or env-dependency (001671) defects, and manifest verify stays unverified.

Both new graded runs fail the same way as the pristine baseline (002661: pytest rc=1, 3 of 8 failing; 001671: collection ImportError, rc=2), so reward 0 shows the attacks did not forge a pass; it does not show the tests would detect a partial fix.
The existing 1.4.0 verdict files (ladder-p0-har244.json, ladder-p0-ranks4-9.json, ladder-p1-ranks10-15.json) are unchanged.
